Maine Mayors Coalition Testimony on LD 177, An Act to Create Municipal Cannabis Revenue Sharing, and LD 347, An Act to Provide Qualifying Municipalities a Percentage of Adult Use
Cannabis Sales Tax and Excise Tax Revenue
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs, the Maine Mayors Coalition is providing testimony in support of LD 177, An Act to Create Municipal Cannabis Revenue Sharing, and LD 347, An Act to Provide Qualifying Municipalities a Percentage of Adult Use Cannabis Sales Tax and Excise Tax Revenue.
The Maine Mayors Coalition is a nonpartisan group representing the mayors of eleven Maine communities - Auburn, Bangor, Biddeford, Lewiston, Portland, Rockland, Saco, Sanford, South Portland, Waterville and Westbrook - and nearly 300,000 residents. The Coalition advocates on behalf of our citizens and municipalities for policies that recognize the vital services Maine cities provide and the positive impact Maine cities have on our state. The Coalition seeks to work in partnership with state and federal elected officials to meet the needs of Maine people.
Cities permitting adult use cannabis establishments will benefit under both bills. LD 177 directs 10 percent of the funds in the Adult Use Cannabis Public Health and Safety and Municipal Opt-in Fund go equally to these municipalities. LD 347 establishes a new fund requiring 12 percent of the revenue from sales and excise taxes on adult use cannabis be distributed to the municipalities.
Like you, we make every effort to keep property taxes as low as possible while providing our citizens with necessary municipal services. Rising costs and spiking property values in recent years have made this much more difficult. And, it is Maine property owners who pay the price with higher property taxes.
The new income streams included in both bills will provide our cities with additional financial resources that will help us meet our municipal obligations. In turn, our homeowners and businesses would see property tax relief through a reduction in the municipal tax levy.
We respectfully ask you to support LD 177 and LD 347. Thank you for your time.
10032830:
MAINE SERVICE CENTERS COALITION
60 Community Drive  Augusta, Maine 04330  (207) 623-8428
Testimony of the Maine Service Centers Coalition LD 177, An Act to Create Municipal Cannabis Revenue Sharing, and LD 347, An Act to Provide Qualifying Municipalities a Percentage of Adult Use
Cannabis Sales Tax and Excise Tax Revenue
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and esteemed members of the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs, the Maine Service Centers Coalition is submitting testimony in support of LD 177, An Act to Create Municipal Cannabis Revenue Sharing, and LD 347, An Act to Provide Qualifying Municipalities a Percentage of Adult Use Cannabis Sales Tax and Excise Tax Revenue.
The Maine Service Centers Coalition, comprised of 26 towns and cities across the state, articulates the importance of healthy and thriving service center communities, advocates for public policy that supports and contributes to the economic and social viability of our communities, and collaborates with municipal officials, legislators, state agencies and non-profits to pursue quality of life for all who live and work in our state.
We are supporting LD 177 and LD 347 as both provide welcome sources of funding for cities and towns with adult use cannabis establishments. Under LD 177, these municipalities would receive 10 percent of the Adult Use Cannabis Public Health and Safety and Municipal Opt-in Fund. Under LD 347, the municipalities would receive 12 percent of the revenue from the sales and excise taxes on adult use cannabis and corresponding products.
Both bills guarantee additional revenues would flow to cities and towns already providing municipal services to adult cannabis establishments. The new funds would allow these municipalities to continue to meet their obligations to all their citizens and, importantly, reduce the property tax burdens that now fall squarely onto homeowners and businesses.
For these reasons, we ask you to give every consideration to supporting LD 177 and LD 347.
Thank you for your time and attention.
10032773:
Testimony of the Maine Municipal Association
In Support of
LD 177 - An Act to Create Municipal Cannabis Revenue Sharing & LD 347 - An Act to Provide Qualifying Municipalities a Percentage of Adult Use Cannabis Sales Tax and Excise Tax Revenue
February 12, 2025
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and members of the Veterans and Legal Affairs Committee, my name is Rebecca Lambert, and I am providing testimony in support of LD 177 and LD 347 on behalf of the Maine Municipal Association's (MMA) elected 70-member Legislative Policy Committee (LPC). For reference, the LPC guides MMA's advocacy efforts and establishes positions on bills of municipal interest.
Municipal officials express strong support for both LD 177 and LD 347 aimed to share a greater portion of cannabis revenue with municipalities who have opted in to allow these businesses within their jurisdictions. They appreciate the recognition and would only suggest disbursing the shared revenue proportionally among the municipalities where the revenue was generated.
When Maine voters approved cannabis legalization, the intent was to create a regulated market that benefits the state and local communities. Municipalities that have opted in to allow cannabis businesses have taken on the responsibilities of zoning, permitting, law enforcement coordination, and public safety oversight, among other duties. These responsibilities require resources, yet under the current system, many of these municipalities do not receive a direct share, except the portion distributed through the traditional revenue sharing program, of the revenue they helped to generate. Local leaders feel it is both fair and necessary to ensure that local governments receive a portion of the revenue generated by the industry they help regulate and support.
Cannabis revenue sharing, in any manner, would provide much-needed financial support for local infrastructure, law enforcement, public health initiatives, and community programs. It would also incentivize more municipalities to participate in the legal cannabis market, expanding access to regulated and tested products while reducing the prevalence of illicit sales. Fair revenue distribution strengthens local economies and ensures the sustainability of Maine's cannabis industry.
Across the country where cannabis legalization has occurred, local governments who have opted into the program have seen the benefit from a portion of the tax revenue. For example, Nevada dedicates 15% of tax revenue to local governments, Massachusetts and California provide for a local option sales tax to be imposed, and in Michigan, 15% of the excise tax is earmarked for county government, with an additional 15% for municipalities--equating to a nearly $10 million dollar investment in municipal and county governments.
LD 177 and LD 347 have the potential to create a more equitable system that benefits both the state and the communities that make this industry possible. Thank you for your commitment to ensuring a fair and sustainable future for Maine's cannabis industry and the municipalities who support it. I appreciate your time and consideration of the municipal perspective.
